assessment.nobel_worthiness: A defining empirical account of how trade and technological change reshape local labour markets, tasks, and inequality, with unusually broad influence on economic research and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock evidence and its labour-market interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated over a long period, generated substantial follow-on work, and remain central to research on labour-market adjustment.
uncertainties: The relative weight of trade, technology, and other local shocks remains contested.
The broader contribution has several important adjacent contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and made geographic and institutional variation in opportunity a central empirical economic question.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are closely associated with the foundational collaborative research program.
assessment.maturity: The measurement infrastructure and substantive results are extensively used and have supported a large subsequent literature.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation of place-based mobility associations requires care.
The program is comparatively recent relative to some established prize-worthy contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit studies provided compelling, replicable evidence on discrimination and reshaped empirical work on labour-market inequality.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are the clearest central credit for the landmark correspondence-study contribution.
assessment.maturity: The designs have been widely adopted, scrutinized, and extended across labour markets and countries.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify specific hiring-stage mechanisms rather than all forms of discrimination.
The broader methodological tradition has many contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions established that health, environment, and childhood investments have persistent economic consequences and materially changed human-capital research.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and dynamic skill-formation foundations of the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base is deep, spans many shocks and settings, and has influenced health, education, and policy research.
uncertainties: The candidate formulation combines related but analytically distinct research programs.
Long-run mechanisms and policy transportability vary across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony made imperfect competition in labour markets a practical framework for understanding wages, employer power, and policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied a central theoretical synthesis, while Ashenfelter and Naidu are important to empirical development and application.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a major organizing lens in labour economics and has stimulated extensive empirical testing.
uncertainties: The scope and magnitude of monopsony power differ substantially across labour markets.
Credit for the theoretical and empirical revival is diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on teacher quality, educational production, and accountability established education as a measurable field of economic policy evaluation with large long-run stakes.
assessment.attribution: Hanushek, Kane, and Woessmann provide strong coverage of the principal research strands, though credit is inherently broad.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has been tested through extensive administrative-data and policy research over decades.
uncertainties: Accountability and value-added estimates remain sensitive to institutional design and measurement choices.
Attribution within the broad education-production literature is difficult to delimit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of adverse-selection theory with credible measurement substantially advanced understanding of insurance markets and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie are prominent contributors to the theory-measurement connection.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and influential across health, credit, and insurance economics.
uncertainties: The contribution encompasses several related theoretical and empirical strands.
Selection and welfare conclusions can be context dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Legal-origins research made investor protection and institutional design central explanations for differences in financial development and corporate governance.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, and Shleifer are central authors of the core cross-country research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has had enduring influence and generated extensive empirical and theoretical debate.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation of legal-origin comparisons remains debated.
The appropriate scope of credit within the larger law-and-finance literature is uncertain.
